First of all, as a very introverted person, I certainly feel the need for a safe space from time to time. Now, before you start pumping that down arrow like a boy who just discovered masturbation, please let me explain. Everyone needs and deserves a safe space from time to time, and most people already have them. These spaces are commonly called your bedroom, your house, or your car. You have every right to demand certain things from those that choose to interact with you on your own private property. Sure, they may then choose not to interact with you, but that is also their right.

However, the minute you step out of those acceptable safe spaces, you have absolutely no right to insist that other's curtail their behavior for your comfort. Your rights in no way supersede (no matter what the average SJW thinks) anyone else's rights. If you can't accept the way the world works, by all means, please (Please!) stay in your acceptable safe spaces: your room, your house and your car. You can choose to close your mind to ideas and opinions that make you uncomfortable, but you have no ability to close someone else's mouth. Or at least you shouldn't, and I really hope the recent backlash on college campuses gets rid of this ridiculous culture of "a right to not be offended" that so many have tried to force us to adopt.

The 1946 Aleutian Islands earthquake occurred near Alaska on April 1, 1946 with a magnitude of 8.6. It resulted in 165–173 casualties and over $26 million in damage. This prompted the creation of the Seismic Sea Wave Warning System, which later became the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center in 1949.
